clues: This small town sits in the Karoo region in South Africa. It lies in the Northern Cape, in the north of the land.
The river bed here stays dry most of the time. When good rains fall, the water can rush in as floods.
In the 1800s, a trekboer settler came to this spot. He camped and settled beside the dry river bed.
In 1961, a flood swept through this place. The flood split the whole settlement in two.
Local land around here has a telling name. People call this dry part the Thirst Land.
